protected_paths.description: Workspace-relative paths to mount read-only. Replaces the defaults when set.

additional_protected_paths.description: Extra paths to protect in addition to the defaults

writable_paths.description: Workspace-relative paths to REMOVE from the effective protected set (e.g. to let a tool manage its own settings file). A protection downgrade, so it is honored only from trusted-scope config (~/.coi/config.toml or $COI_CONFIG), never from an untrusted project config.

secret_paths.description: Workspace-relative globs to MASK inside the container: each match is mounted read-only over an empty file/dir so the agent can neither read nor modify it (e.g. [".env", "*.pem", "secrets/**"]). Additive protection — honored from any scope; merges as a union.

disable_protection.description: Disable all read-only path protection (not recommended)

host_immutable.description: Apply the Linux immutable attribute (chattr +i) to protected paths on the host before container start. Prevents the unshare+umount bypass. Default: true.

reduce_kernel_surface.description: Kernel attack-surface hardening: disables Docker/nesting support (wins over [container] docker) and denies the syscall families behind most recent kernel escape chains (io_uring, bpf, userfaultfd, keyring) via security.syscalls.deny. The container still shares the host kernel — this narrows the boundary, it does not make it escape-proof. Default: false. Trusted scope only. Enabled by the built-in 'hardened' profile.

reduce_kernel_surface_strict.description: Opt-in STRICT tier on top of reduce_kernel_surface: additionally denies perf_event_open (a long-standing kernel-LPE vector). Kept separate because, unlike the base list, denying perf_event_open removes real capability — kernel-level profiling (perf, JVM async-profiler's perf mode) stops working, though it degrades gracefully (EPERM, no crash). Enabling it implies reduce_kernel_surface. Default: false. Trusted scope only.
